race_context: The district: South Vermillion Community School Corporation, based in Clinton, operates South Vermillion High School, South Vermillion Middle School, Central Elementary and Van Duyn Elementary {sv_board}. Superintendent Dr. Micah Williams, a former SVMS teacher and the district's assistant superintendent since August 2023, was promoted to superintendent in July 2025 {sv_supt}; he succeeded Dave Chapman, who had led the district since 2008 {wtwo_sv_supt}. In August 2026 Williams reported that enrollment came in below the district's projection of about 1,550 students and was lower than the prior year {sv_min_2026_08}.

The board has seven members {sv_board}{sv_min_2023_01}. Seats are tied to residence areas, Clinton City, Clinton Township, Helt Township and one at-large seat, with Clinton City, Clinton Township and Helt Township seats elected in 2024 and the at-large seat plus one seat from each of the three areas elected in 2022 {vc_2022}{vc_2024}. The 2026 sample ballot for a Clinton City precinct includes all four South Vermillion races, each 'Vote For One (1) Only' {vc_sample}. Current members are John Paul Roehm (president), Kelli Hill (vice president), Jon Beardsley (secretary), Jeff Goeppner, Jeff Sisson, Brandae Stateler and Bruce West (legislative liaison) {sv_board}{sv_min_2026_01}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: four seats, one each for At Large, Clinton City, Clinton Township and Helt Township, matching the state list {in_list}{vc_sample}. Three incumbents are running again: Jeff Sisson (At Large, elected 2022 over Christina M. Barnes), Brandae Stateler (Clinton Township, elected 2022 over Jon E. Beardsley, 1,532 to 1,500) and board president John Paul Roehm (Helt Township, unopposed in 2022) {vc_2022}{vc_2022_list}.

Clinton City seat: no candidate filed for the Clinton City seat in 2022 {vc_2022}. At the January 2023 reorganization, Roehm stated that Beardsley was 'a holdover member from his previous appointment on the board' and did not need to be sworn in {sv_min_2023_01}. The minutes do not name Beardsley's seat; that he holds this Clinton City seat is an inference. Beardsley is not on the 2026 ballot, so the Clinton City race between Bryan Alan Lemmons and Meghan L. Bell will seat a new member {in_list}.

The district's other Clinton City seat, won in 2024 by Jerry Hawkins, became vacant in 2025 {vc_2024}{sv_min_2025_08}. On Aug. 20, 2025, after interviewing five applicants, including 2026 candidate Bryan Lemmons, the board appointed Jeff Goeppner 3–2 over Nick Hall {sv_min_2025_08}. Williams said that appointment runs through the remainder of Hawkins' term, which expires in 2028 {sv_min_2025_08}.

School reconfiguration (2026): at public information meetings on June 10 and June 24, 2026, Williams presented options to renovate Central and Van Duyn elementaries or to reconfigure the district into a PK–6 building and a 7–12 building on one campus for the 2029–2030 school year; he said current school capacity use is 52.89% {sv_min_2026_06}{sv_plan}. The district's FAQ says either option would use the same bonding capacity in 2028 and that overall tax rates would not be affected. It also says no staff would lose their jobs because of the reconfiguration, and it lists plans to bring back elementary art and add grade 2 high-ability programming {sv_faq}. Residents at the June 10 meeting raised traffic concerns at Wildcat Drive and IN-63, and Williams said he would follow up with INDOT {sv_min_2026_06}{sv_faq}. The board had discussed school consolidation in executive session on Dec. 1, 2025 {sv_min_2025_12}.

Budget (2025–2026): the 2026 budget cut the Education Fund by about $500,000, held the Operations Fund level, and raised the Debt Service Fund by about $300,000 to speed up planned debt repayment {sv_min_2025_09}. The proposed 2027 budget, advertised in August 2026, includes an Education Fund of about $12.72 million, about $1.3 million of which is planned for transfer to the Operations Fund; an Operations Fund of about $5.35 million with an advertised levy of about $4.6 million; and a debt service levy of $3 million {sv_min_2026_08}. Assessed valuation was reported at about $671.1 million, up about 1.31%, and the public hearing was set for Sept. 1, 2026 {sv_min_2026_08}. The board approved a 2026–27 classified employee handbook that includes a 2% increase in the compensation model {sv_min_2026_06}.

Enrollment (August 2026): Williams said the enrollment drop is expected to reduce projected funding, partly offset by an increase in state per-student funding, and that no elementary class exceeded about 22 students {sv_min_2026_08}.

Academics (August 2026): the district reported 2026 IREAD pass rates of about 98.2% at Van Duyn Elementary and about 76.7% at Central Elementary, and outlined Orton-Gillingham training and intervention steps for Central {sv_min_2026_08}.

Policies (2026): in June 2026 the board adopted policy updates requiring students to keep personal devices stored during instructional time, in line with new state law {sv_min_2026_06}. In August 2026 the district moved to two athletic directors sharing oversight of grades 5–12 {sv_min_2026_08}.

Forums: no candidate forum, questionnaire or news coverage of the 2026 South Vermillion races was found. The only recorded statements from challengers are Bryan Lemmons' August 2025 appointment interview and his July 2026 public comment to the board {sv_min_2025_08}{sv_min_2026_07}.

items: In his 2025 interview said board members should ensure curriculum follows state and board of education requirements and should raise academic standards to challenge students {sv_min_2025_08}.
Supported hands-on learning for future educators, with students involved in teaching {sv_min_2025_08}.

In a July 16, 2026 public comment to the board, identified as a board candidate, he called for added procedures and protocols for hiring coaches, more transparency in coach selection, and evaluation of coaching effectiveness {sv_min_2026_07}.

In 2025 said that when residents bring concerns he would listen and write them down without making promises, and would separate valid from invalid points before bringing them to the board {sv_min_2025_08}.
Said he would accept majority board decisions he disagreed with {sv_min_2025_08}.

on_incumbent: At the July 2026 meeting he raised concerns about the district's coaching hiring practices, declining participation in athletic programs, and parents' concerns that athletes were discouraged or penalized for family vacations during seasons. He said his comments were meant to encourage positive changes {sv_min_2026_07}. The board adopted a new 5–12 athletic director structure the next month; the minutes do not tie that change to his comments {sv_min_2026_08}.
plans: In his 2025 interview said his first-year priority would be boosting student morale, including encouraging participation in school events and sports and connecting community involvement with school activities {sv_min_2025_08}.
